JOB PURPOSE

This role exists to drive category and channel growth by transforming shopper, customer and market insights into winning commercial strategies and trade marketing plans that accelerate profitable growth for both Unilever and its retail partners. The Trade Marketing Manager plays a critical role in connecting category and brand ambitions with customer needs, ensuring best-in-class execution across channels while strengthening Unilever’s leadership position in the Foods category.

You’ll be part of a team that believes in doing work that matters — for people and the planet.

Because here, we don’t just hire for jobs. We invite you to be part of something bigger.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
- Develop and implement customer, channel, and category growth strategies aligned with business objectives and category priorities.
- Translate category and brand ambitions into actionable commercial plans that drive sustainable and profitable growth.
- Leverage shopper, customer, and market insights to identify growth opportunities, mitigate risks, and inform strategic decision-making.
- Create compelling category and portfolio selling stories that strengthen customer partnerships and support business growth.
- Design and execute shopper-centric trade marketing programs that increase brand penetration, visibility, and category performance.
- Drive excellence across key commercial levers including promotions, assortment, merchandising, and in-store execution.
- Partner with Customer Development teams to build and support Joint Business Plans, category reviews, and customer growth initiatives.
- Monitor category, customer, and channel performance, evaluating trade investment effectiveness and recommending optimization opportunities.

- Champion a customer-centric and shopper-first mindset while fostering collaboration and alignment across stakeholders.

- Minimum 2 years of experience in Trade Marketing, or related commercial functions.
- Proven experience working with major modern trade customers and supporting customer growth strategies.
- Strong understanding of category management principles, shopper behavior, and trade marketing execution.
- Demonstrated ability to translate data and insights into actionable commercial recommendations and business plans.
- Bachelor's degree in Business, Economics, Marketing, or a related field, with fluency in both English and Polish.

- Experience supporting Joint Business Planning and strategic customer engagements within a leading FMCG organization.
- Advanced analytical and storytelling skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders through data-driven recommendations.
- Proven track record of leading cross-functional projects and driving business results in complex, matrix environments.

- Opportunities for the development and improvement of qualifications

- Benefits: car, life insurance, private medical care, pension fund, sharing the cost of sports activities, Benefits System – Cafeteria and many others

About the Role
We are looking for an experienced and results-driven Area Sales Manager to lead and manage a large sales team across an assigned geographical area.

The role is responsible for driving sales growth, strengthening product distribution and visibility, optimizing outlet coverage and territory management, and increasing market share.

The ideal candidate brings strong leadership and commercial capabilities, with a solid understanding of FMCG sales operations, distributor management, working capital, and ROI .

Sales Strategy & Execution
- Develop and execute sales strategies by translating monthly Customer Development priorities and company strategy into strong market execution.
- Set sales targets and objectives for the assigned area and closely monitor performance against targets.
- Provide clear direction and support to Unilever and distributor sales teams to identify opportunities and drive sales.
- Conduct regular market visits to monitor product availability, visibility, promotions, and monthly campaign execution.

- Analyze sales and market data across channels and categories to identify gaps, trends, and growth opportunities.

- Distributors and retailers

Burton and Crumlin are two important Unilever Foods sourcing units in the UK, with complementary portfolios and distinct operational priorities & delivering a combined turnover of €320m. Burton is a UK Condiments and Marmite site, producing products across brands including Hellmann's, Marmite, Bovril and Colman's. Crumlin is the UK Pot Noodle site and has an important role in the Mini Meals portfolio. Together, the sites represent a broad and dynamic finance scope, with ongoing focus on operational performance, cost competitiveness, investment delivery, controls and transformation.

Main purpose of the job:

The Burton and Crumlin Industrial Finance Manager position is a great opportunity to further develop in three crucial parts of any finance leadership position: Business partnering, controlling and FP&A. As finance manager for two factories, you are part of both the Burton and Crumlin leadership teams, supporting and contributing to the decision-making process across the two sites.
The role requires the ability to balance priorities across two different operations, build strong relationships with both site teams and provide a joined-up financial view where relevant. You are taking active part in shaping the future of both sites, not only as a finance expert but also as an LT member responsible for quality of products, safety and wellbeing of employees and the factories' CSR agenda.
You provide decision making support to both LTs, prepare the financial appraisal for investments and drive the savings agenda across Burton and Crumlin. The finance manager is also accountable for keeping compliance of both sites to the Unilever control framework and audit requirements.
The role is part of a European team of Industrial Finance Business Partners and reports into the Foods Network lead for Europe. On main accounting, controlling and reporting tasks the FM is supported by the site finance resources, a make expertise team (MET) and shared services teams (SCFS, OC, IBM).

WORK SUMMARY / RESPONSIBILITIES
• Business partnering both Factory Leadership Teams to drive site performance
• Responsible for projects governance and delivery of in-year financial performance (costs/capex/waste/savings) across Burton and Crumlin
• Responsible to ensure site on-ground controls are executed at both sites (inventories, purchase process, IFRS 16, balance sheet etc)
• Co-creates and co-drives the savings agenda with operations across both sites and uses available industrial tools to support (ZBB, benchmarking)
• Budget Planning, Forecasting, weekly cost governance & Month End Activities for Burton and Crumlin
• Drives long term strategic planning for both sites (Masterplan and BP) guiding the site leadership teams on the key value items
• Supports decision making for strategic and cross-site projects with ad hoc data/analysis
• Supports in the design and implementation of transformation plans for the Foods network
• Participate in central projects to build finance capabilities for other sites of the cluster/ network.

RESOURCE TO BE MANAGED UNDER POSITIONS AUTHORITY

• 2 Direct reports; one at each site

MAIN INTERACTIONS

a) Burton and Crumlin factory teams
• Leadership team (Director, HR, Planning Manager, Operations Manager, Manex Manager, Engineering Manager, Repairs & Maintenance Manager, Quality Manager, Safety Manager and Site Services Manager)
• Project leaders (engineers and specialists)
The FBP actively interacts with both site leadership teams and operations on performance, controls and decisions, ensuring appropriate focus on each site while identifying opportunities for alignment and sharing best practices.

b) European central teams
• Foods Make network lead and the Foods central finance team
• VP Supply chain Foods (performance reviews and analysis)
• Foods P&I / Planning Teams
• Shared resources (MET / OC/ SCFS)
• Local MSO finance team in case of specific local finance/business projects.

KEY SKILLS REQUIRED

• Strong business partnering skills, with the ability to influence and challenge Factory Leadership Teams and operational stakeholders
• Strong financial planning and analytical capability, with the ability to translate complex financial information into clear operational actions
• Ability to manage priorities across two sites, maintaining sufficient focus on each operation while identifying cross-site opportunities and synergies
• Solid understanding of factory finance, including production costs, savings, capex, waste, forecasting, month end and financial controls
• Ability to lead the financial appraisal and governance of investments, transformation projects and performance improvement initiatives
• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the confidence to work across site, country and European teams
• High level of ownership, accuracy and control mindset, combined with a practical and solution-oriented approach
• Ability to develop finance capability within the site teams and make effective use of MET and shared service support

Behavioural and Leadership Requirements:

• Acts as a strong and visible finance leader across both sites, building trust with the Factory Leadership Teams and wider site organisations
• Demonstrates passion for high performance and continuous improvement, setting clear expectations and following through on commitments
• Influences and challenges constructively, bringing an independent finance perspective while remaining practical and solution oriented
• Balances priorities across Burton and Crumlin, making clear choices and maintaining appropriate leadership presence at both sites
• Leads through collaboration, creates alignment across functions and encourages sharing of best practices between the two sites
• Develops and coaches finance team members and supports stronger financial capability within the operational teams
• Communicates with clarity and confidence, adapting the message for factory teams, senior leadership and European stakeholders
• Demonstrates curiosity, resilience and personal accountability, particularly when managing change, ambiguity and competing priorities
• Role models integrity, a strong control mindset and commitment to quality, safety and employee wellbeing

Mobility requirements:

Role based in Burton site in UK, with regular presence and travel between Burton and Crumlin

Professional qualifications and experience:

Finance, Accounting or Business degree, or equivalent professional experience.
A recognised professional accounting qualification is preferred.
Typically, 5+ years of relevant Finance experience, ideally including business partnering in a manufacturing or production environment. Demonstrated experience in financial planning, performance management, controls and investment appraisal would be an advantage.
Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with operational and senior stakeholders.
Fluency in English.

Cyber criminals advertise fake job adverts with prestigious employers as a way of stealing information or even defrauding individuals out of money. Many of Unilever’s recruitment sites publish a warning to candidates about recruitment fraud. The Cyber Security team also proactively scan for signs of people setting up fake Unilever sites and act to close them down.

ABOUT UNILEVER
With 3.4 billion people in over 190 countries using our products every day, Unilever is a business that makes a real impact on the world. Work on brands that are loved and improve the lives of our consumers and the communities around us. We are driven by our purpose: to make sustainable living commonplace, and it is our belief that doing business the right way drives superior performance. At the heart of what we do is our people – we believe that when our people work with purpose, we will create a better business and a better world.

JOB PURPOSE
The Head of Sales, Core Grocery & Club, is responsible for developing and executing Unilever Foods' commercial strategy across a diverse portfolio of grocery, club, and wholesale customers. This leader is accountable for delivering sustainable volume, share, and profit growth while leading a cross-functional organization to strengthen customer partnerships, enhance commercial effectiveness, and accelerate business performance across multiple channels. The role requires balancing enterprise priorities with unique customer needs while creating scalable strategies that drive long-term growth.

WHAT WILL YOUR MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES BE

- Lead Unilever Foods' strategy and execution across a portfolio of grocery, club, and wholesale customers.
- Develop and deliver customer growth strategies through Joint Business Planning, customer partnerships, and market-leading commercial execution.
- Partner closely with Marketing, Customer Strategy & Planning (CSP), Category Management, Shopper Insights, Revenue Growth Management, Finance, and Supply Chain teams to deliver sustainable growth.

Job Title: UFH Program & Operations Manager
Location: Trumbull R&D, CT

Want to Change The World?
Unilever is one of the world’s leading suppliers of Beauty, Personal and Home Care products selling in over 190 countries and used by 3.7 billion consumers every day. Unilever has more than 400 brands used in homes around the world, including Dove, Sure, TRESemmé, Sunsilk, Vaseline, Comfort, Persil and Surf. As one of the world’s largest users of fragrances, we recognise that creating exceptional fragrances is at the heart of delivering extraordinary consumer experiences and driving desire at scale.

To achieve our ambition, Unilever Fragrance House (UFH) is undertaking a global fragrance transformation, leveraging expert inhouse fragrance teams to craft unmissably superior fragrances for our Personal Care, Beauty & Wellbeing and Home Care Business Groups.

Job Purpose
We have an exciting opportunity for a Program & Operations Manager to join the UFH US Hub, playing a pivotal role in bringing the next generation of fragrances to life for Unilever's global brands.

As the operational heartbeat of the US Hub, you will lead the successful delivery of fragrance innovation programmes, ensuring projects progress seamlessly from creation through to submission readiness. Working at the intersection of perfumery, science, innovation and operations, you will coordinate cross-functional teams, manage complex project portfolios, and ensure fragrance oils, applications and evaluations are delivered on time, in full, and to the highest quality standards.

This is a highly visible role that combines program leadership, operational excellence and people management. Partnering closely with Perfumers, Evaluators, R&D teams and Business Group stakeholders, you will drive prioritisation, remove bottlenecks, and create the conditions for teams to deliver exceptional fragrances that delight consumers across the Americas.

Beyond program delivery, you will play a key role in shaping the future capability of the US Hub. From leading laboratory operations and developing team capability, to driving digitalisation, data management and continuous improvement initiatives, you will help build a high-performing fragrance organisation that is equipped to support future growth. You will also oversee facilities, resource planning and laboratory readiness, ensuring the hub has the people, processes and infrastructure needed to succeed.
This role is ideal for a collaborative and hands-on leader who thrives in a fast-paced, innovation-driven environment and is passionate about turning ideas into consumer-ready fragrance experiences.

Job Title: People Operations Specialist - Foods (Fixed-Term Contract)
Location: BGC Office (Hybrid)

JOB PURPOSE

The People Operations Specialist is an expert in Workday employee data management and Hire-to-Retire processes, role changes and exits within the assigned markets. This role manages high-volume activities, resolves cases from ServiceNow, and ensures Workday remains accurate and up to date.

You'll be part of a team that believes in doing work that matters - for people and the planet. Because here, we don't just hire for jobs. We invite you to be part of something bigger.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

- Workday Employee Data Management:
- Hires: - Set up Workday profiles for new hires from recruitment (internal appointments and external hires).
- Generate required business letters and contracts.
- Manage cancellations for declined offers or no-shows.
- Support on completing joiner checklist steps.

- Role Changes/Promotions/Exits: - Process employee moves, promotions and exits in Workday, ensuring data accuracy across elements (i.e. cost center).
- Coordinate case closure with stakeholders and in-market partners.
- Initiate EIB uploads for mass data changes.
- Provide Workday data support to stakeholders as required.

- Pay & Benefits Management: - Collaborate to maintain accurate compensation data into payroll systems.
- Support of enrolment and derolment of benefits, including coordination across journeys to ensure OTIF processing.

- Exit Management: - Execute voluntary and involuntary employee terminations in Workday, including Reduction in Force (steps that are not self-served).
- Collaborate with in-market partners for seamless exits and clearances.
- Handle severance administration.

- Validation of the Transferring Population: - Validate the movement of employees; reconciling each record against source data to confirm employees have been moved correctly in Workday.
o Perform data-integrity checks on key elements after transfer (position, cost center, work unit, line manager, compensation, organisational assignment) and resolve discrepancies before sign-off.
- Compare expected versus completed transfers, log exceptions, and maintain evidence of validation for governance and control.
o Raise and track defects through to closure, re-checking corrected records and confirming resolution.
- Effective Systems Integration
- Manage integration between Joiner-Mover-Leaver processes and Workday (automated/manual triggers).
- Create and update local SOPs and work instructions.
- Proactively flag technical issues to relevant stakeholders to mitigate employee experience disruptions.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
- Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field (preferred).
- Proven experience in customer service, employee experience, shared service centers, HR advisory, HR partnering.
- Familiarity with HR processes and policies, ideally in multi-country or regional operations.
- Proficiency in Workday and ServiceNow (or similar systems like SAP).
- Experience supporting a data migration, mergers & acquisitions, separation or mass-change programme is an advantage.

SKILLS
- Required proficiency in English
- Understanding of Agile ways of working.
- Strong written communication skills, capable of delivering clear and concise real-time information
- Providing consistent feedback and stakeholder management
- Advanced Excel proficiency and ability to turn data into action.
- Excellent problem-solving skills and customer-centric mindset.
- Demonstrated multitasking and prioritization skills in fast-paced environments.
- Commitment to quality, accuracy and adherence to SLAs.
- Effective team collaboration across global hubs/locations, including with third-party teams.
- Effective Project Management skills.
- Adaptability to new technologies and systems.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
- Confident navigating Workday to verify transactions, run and interpret reports, and validate business processes end-to-end.
- Advanced Excel (lookups, pivot tables, large-file comparison) to reconcile VR outputs against source data at scale.
- Ability to prepare, load and validate EIB templates for bulk data changes, with disciplined error-checking.
- Understanding of data-privacy and control requirements (segregation of duties, evidence, sign-off) in a shared-tenant environment.
- Comfortable using tracker/RAID logs and Gantt charts to manage a concentrated, milestone-driven workload.

BEHAVIORS
- You are energized by delivering with excellence, taking personal ownership through building resilience and taking care of your own wellbeing.
- You are relentless on prioritization and focusing on what counts, making maximum performance impact in areas you touch.
- You are constantly staying three steps ahead on ways to do things differently, interpreting data, spotting issues and opportunities; whilst caring deeply about what Consumer and Customers need.
